sections.html:
Amherst is Buffalo's biggest suburb, up in the north of Erie County. About 130,442 people lived here in mid-2025, in 53,343 households. Owners live in 69.9% of homes, and a typical owned home is valued at $311,600. Owners with a mortgage pay about $1,945 a month, and typical gross rent is $1,393.

Over one resident in five is 65 or older, and 86.4% were at the same address a year earlier. Long tenure like that often ends in a downsize or an estate sale, and many of the town's subdivisions are decades old. A financed buyer may ask for repairs to kitchens, baths and mechanical systems. A cash buyer will usually fold them into the price.

sections.h2: Hamlets, the village and mailing addresses
sections.html:
Most names on an Amherst address are hamlets or post-office areas with no government of their own. Williamsville is the exception, an incorporated village inside the town.

  • Eggertsville and Snyder, in the older southwest, near Buffalo
  • Williamsville, the incorporated village in the south
  • Getzville and the Audubon area, near the center
  • East Amherst and Swormville, shared with the Town of Clarence
  • North Bailey, around Bailey Avenue and Maple Road

Villages and hamlets also differ in who answers the phone for permits and local rules. Before you list or accept an offer, confirm with the town whether the parcel falls under a village office as well.

Mailing addresses can cross town lines. Some homes east of Transit Road carry a Williamsville address yet belong to the Town of Clarence for taxes and schools. Read the tax bill to see which municipality applies before you write any paperwork.

sections.h2: Which school district is your house in?
sections.html:
Four public districts divide the town. Williamsville Central takes the eastern half and some of Clarence. Amherst Central has the southwest, around Eggertsville and Snyder. Sweet Home Central has the northwest, including West Amherst and Getzville, and Clarence Central has a small southeastern corner.

Two homes sharing a ZIP code can fall in different districts, so name the district whenever you describe the house. The tax bill names it, and the Assessor's Office can confirm.

sections.h2: Rental registration when tenants live in the house
sections.html:
Chapter 44 of the town code bars renting a unit until the owner holds a rental registration certificate. An owner-occupied property with two or fewer units, if not used for short stays, is exempt.

Amherst rental certificates
Certificate typeLengthFee
Standard rentalUp to three years$75 inspection fee for each unit
Short-term rental (stays of 1 to 30 days)One year, with an annual inspection$250 a unit if the owner lives there, $500 if not (2025 form)
  • No certificate issues until the unit passes inspection and local property taxes are current.
  • Owners living outside Erie, Niagara and Genesee counties need a local agent.
  • Houses built before 1978 carry a lead paint certification on the form.

A buyer can take over a certificate's remaining term by filing a transfer application with the Commissioner of Building within 30 days of the deed, so hand over the certificate and inspection paperwork at closing. Skipping registration can double the fee, add a $75 fine and lead to a notice to vacate. A code violation can bring up to $1,500 or 15 days in jail.

Each parcel is valued by the town Assessor. If you disagree, form RP-524 is free to file. Most communities use the fourth Tuesday in May as the cutoff, which would be May 25 in 2027, so confirm the day with the Assessor's Office at 5583 Main Street in Williamsville. Call ahead, since the office has taken paperwork by mail or drop-off as well as hearings in person.

If you are close to selling, a lower assessment helps the buyer more than it helps you. A wrong square footage or unit count should still be corrected, because an appraiser pulls the same record.

Erie County may foreclose on liens that sit unpaid for two years or longer. Owners receive notice and a final redemption date. To redeem, an owner pays the back taxes plus a $500 statutory fee by cash, certified check, bank check or money order to the County Director of Real Property Tax Services. Parcels not redeemed head to public auction, and later years' taxes keep accruing.

Owe back taxes? Ask Erie County Real Property Tax Services for a payoff number, because fees and interest keep adding to the balance. Sale proceeds can clear the lien, so ask your title company to order that figure soon.

sections.h2: Transfer tax and your sale options
sections.html:
Sellers normally cover New York's conveyance tax, which runs $2 for every $500 of price. File the TP-584 return with the Erie County Clerk within 15 days of handing over the deed.

Three routes are open: hire an agent, sell on your own, or take a cash offer. A listing means showings plus a closing date that follows the buyer's lender. A cash buyer takes the house in its current condition, which suits a rental near the end of its certificate, an inherited house or a parcel with back taxes.

sections.h2: How a sale unfolds in Amherst
sections.html:
Start by deciding which municipality your parcel sits in, since a Williamsville mailing address can still mean Clarence taxes. Next, settle the open items attached to the house: a rental certificate that needs transferring, a code violation, or back taxes owed to the county. The title company will find each of these anyway, and a seller who raises them first controls the conversation.

With a mortgage-backed buyer, an inspection comes first, then an appraisal, and the lender sets the calendar. With a cash buyer, the house is reviewed as it stands and you pick the day. Either way you sign the deed at closing, and the title company settles your mortgage and any unpaid tax out of the proceeds before the return and tax go to the clerk.

A tenant adds one more task. Pass the lease and certificate to the buyer, and make sure the transfer application is filed inside the 30 day window so the registration survives the handover.

sections.h2: What to gather before you sell
sections.html:
• The deed and your lender's payoff statement
  • The latest town and school tax bills
  • Any rental certificate and inspection paperwork
  • A written payoff from Erie County if any back taxes are owed

Bring those four and the title search can start the same day. A cash buyer can name a closing date once the numbers are settled, with no appraisal in the middle.

faqs.q: Does a tenant-occupied Amherst house need a rental certificate at sale?
faqs.a: Registration is the owner's duty while the unit is rented. A buyer can take it over by filing within 30 days of the deed, so hand over the certificate and inspection paperwork.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff for contesting an Amherst assessment?
faqs.a: Most New York communities use the fourth Tuesday in May. Check the exact day with the Amherst Assessor's Office. The form is RP-524, and there is no charge to file.

faqs.q: What happens when county tax liens stay unpaid on an Amherst property?
faqs.a: Erie County can foreclose once liens are two or more years old. Owners receive notice and a last redemption date, with a $500 fee, and anything left unredeemed goes to public auction.

faqs.q: Who pays the state transfer tax on an Amherst sale?
faqs.a: Usually the seller. The rate is $2 for each $500, and a leftover partial $500 counts as a whole one. The Erie County Clerk receives the return within 15 days of the deed.

faqs.q: How do I find which district my Amherst house belongs to?
faqs.a: It is one of Williamsville, Amherst, Sweet Home or Clarence Central, depending on location. The tax bill names it, and the Assessor's Office can confirm.
